info.title: ARCHITECH API
info.description:
API for the ARCHITECH Next.js app. All routes live under `frontend/app/api`.

## Data storage: PostgreSQL
All user data is stored in **PostgreSQL** through Prisma (`@auth/prisma-adapter`, schema in `frontend/prisma/schema.prisma`):

| Table | Written by | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | `POST /api/auth/register`, Google/GitHub first sign-in, `PATCH /api/users/me` | name, email, bcrypt password hash, experience level, avatar |
| `accounts` | Google/GitHub sign-in (Prisma adapter) | linked provider id and OAuth access/refresh tokens |
| `projects` | `PUT /api/projects/{id}` (the canvas syncs automatically) | saved diagrams: title, mode, and the graph as `jsonb` (docs/graph-spec.md) |
| `component_types`, `component_implementations` | `npx prisma db seed` | the component library and the technologies behind each component |

Sign-in itself is stateless (`session.strategy: "jwt"`, required for email/password logins). After sign-in the
browser holds only a signed login token (the `next-auth.session-token` cookie) containing the user's id and
experience level, never the user record itself. Every protected route takes the id from that token and reads or
updates the user in PostgreSQL. The experience level in the token is re-read from PostgreSQL at sign-in and
whenever the frontend calls `update()`. (Because of the JWT strategy, the `sessions` table exists but is not used.)

## Routes
- **Custom:** `POST /api/auth/register`, `PATCH /api/users/me`, `GET /api/github/repos`, `GET /api/projects`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/projects/{id}`
- **NextAuth v4** (`app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`): everything else under `/api/auth/*`, with
  Credentials (email + password), Google and GitHub providers. The sign-in page is `/`.

## Calling protected routes
Sign in at http://localhost:3000 in the same browser first. Pages under `/dashboard/*` and `/workspace/*`
redirect to `/` without a valid login token (`proxy.ts`).

Validates the input, normalizes the email (trimmed and lowercased), checks for an existing
user case-insensitively, hashes the password with bcrypt and inserts a row into the PostgreSQL `users` table.
Does **not** sign the user in; the frontend then calls the credentials sign-in.

patch.summary: Save the signed-in user's experience level
patch.description:
Called at the end of onboarding step 1. Updates `users.experienceLevel` in PostgreSQL.
After this succeeds, the frontend calls NextAuth's
`update()`, which re-reads the level into the session token.

get.summary: List the signed-in user's 3 most recently updated GitHub repos
get.description:
Reads the GitHub OAuth access token from the user's `github` row in the PostgreSQL `accounts` table and calls
`GET https://api.github.com/user/repos?sort=updated&per_page=3`. The GitHub response is passed
through unchanged, so each item is a full GitHub repository object; only common fields are listed below.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description:
This is what `signIn("credentials", {...})` posts to. Get `csrfToken` from `/api/auth/csrf` first.

Server steps (`authorize` in route.ts):
1. Rejects a missing or malformed email or password.
2. Normalizes the email (trimmed and lowercased) and looks up the user in PostgreSQL `users`, case-insensitively.
3. Rejects users with no `passwordHash` (Google/GitHub-only accounts).
4. Compares the password with the stored bcrypt hash.
5. On success, issues the login token with the user's `id` and `experienceLevel` (read from PostgreSQL).

Every failure returns the same message, "Invalid email or password", so the response never reveals
whether an email is registered. With `json=true` the error comes back in `{ url }` as `?error=...`;
`signIn(..., { redirect: false })` surfaces it as `result.error`.

json.description: Return JSON `{ url }` instead of a redirect

302.description: Redirect to callbackUrl (success) or the error page

get.summary: OAuth callback (called by Google or GitHub, not by the app)
get.description:
Register these as the redirect URIs in the Google and GitHub OAuth app settings:
`http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google` and `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/github`.

302.description:
On first sign-in the Prisma adapter inserts a row into PostgreSQL `users` (name, email, image)
and one into `accounts` (provider id and OAuth tokens). Later sign-ins reuse them.
Sets the login token and redirects to callbackUrl.
Clears the session cookie and redirects

get.description: Every project of the signed-in user, most recently changed first. Stored in the PostgreSQL `projects` table, one row per project with the diagram in a `jsonb` column.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Project id, generated by the browser (UUID). Letters, digits, '-' and '_', at most 100 characters.

404.description: No project with this id belongs to the user (another user's project is also reported as not found)

put.description:
Creates the project with this id, or replaces it if the user already has it. The browser generates the id, so creating offline and retrying a failed save are both safe: sending the same project twice stores it once.

The diagram is validated against docs/graph-spec.md (section 5): known component types, labels of 1-60 characters, unique node and edge ids, edges between existing nodes, no self-connections or repeated connections, settings within each component's range, and `data.implementation` must exist and belong to the node's type. At most 500 nodes and 2,000 edges.

The canvas calls this automatically: every change is synced in the background.

400.description: Invalid id or body. The message names the first problem and where it is.

value.error: graph.nodes[0].data.type "firewall" is not a known component type.
graph.edges[0].target must be the id of a node in this graph.
graph.edges[0] connects a node to itself.
graph.nodes[1].data.properties.replicas: Replicas must be at most 1000.
Implementation "redis" is a cache, not a database.

404.description: The id belongs to another user's project
No project with this id belongs to the user

post.summary: Build a design from a GitHub repository
post.description:
Uses the GitHub account the user connected at sign-in (its token in the `accounts` table) to read the repository through GitHub's GraphQL API (`POST https://api.github.com/graphql`): one query for the top-level file list and stack files, and one for the same files in up to 8 top-level folders (monorepos).

Stack files read: package.json, docker-compose.yml / compose.yml, prisma/schema.prisma, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, build.gradle.

Detection rules map what they use to components and technologies (for example `next` → Web App (Next.js), `ioredis` → Cache (Redis), `@apollo/server` → API (GraphQL), a `postgres` image → Database (PostgreSQL)), each with its evidence. The design is laid out left to right with typical connections, validated against docs/graph-spec.md and saved as a new project (`source: "github"`, opens in free play). Connections are a best guess to adjust on the canvas.

Technologies the repository uses that ARCHITECH does not model (for example a Traefik or ClickHouse service, or a .NET worker) are returned as `customTechnologies` and saved with the project, so they appear in its sidebar under "From your repo" and can be dragged onto the canvas as unmeasured custom components. A repository with only such technologies still imports.

201.description: The new project and what was detected.

401.description: Not signed in, or the GitHub authorization expired (reconnect GitHub).

404.description: No GitHub account connected, or the repository was not found / is not visible to the account.

409.description: The linked GitHub account has no access token.

422.description: Neither recognizable components nor unmodeled stacks/services were found.

post.summary: Ask the AI Architect about a design (streamed)
post.description:
Validates the design like a saved project, evaluates it with the metrics engine at the given traffic (as Run Design does), and asks the configured model (Claude or Groq). The prompt contains the design (component ids, technologies, settings, connections), the evaluation (scores, metrics, per-component load, findings), the component library and the user's experience level.

With `focus`, the prompt also gets the selected part (its components with their load, the connections inside it, and every connection in from and out to the rest of the design) and the answer is about that part only.

The model can propose changes with a tool; each is checked against the design (graph spec rules) and previewed with the engine (score, capacity, p95, cost, uptime before and after) before it is sent. The canvas applies a suggestion with the same function (src/lib/ai/changes.ts) as one undo step.

The response is newline-delimited JSON (`application/x-ndjson`), one `ChatEvent` per line: `text` parts of the answer, `suggestion`s, `note`s for proposed changes that could not be used, and finally `done` (or `error` if the model stopped part-way).

Limits (model calls; cached answers and failed calls do not count): 5 a minute and 50 a day per user (AI_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, AI_LIMIT_PER_DAY), and 1000 a day for the whole app (AI_LIMIT_GLOBAL_PER_DAY). Windows slide (the last 60 seconds / 24 hours). Reserving a question is atomic, so simultaneous questions cannot slip past a limit. If the AI provider fails or is busy, the question is refunded. Every response carries `X-AI-Remaining-Today` and `X-AI-Limit-Per-Day`.

The same design + conversation (+ focus) within 24 hours is answered from a cache (header `X-AI-Cache: hit`) without calling the model or counting toward the limits. Layout (positions, edge ids) does not affect the cache. Old cache entries and usage rows are deleted about once an hour.

Server configuration: AI_PROVIDER = anthropic | groq (if unset: Anthropic when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else Groq when GROQ_API_KEY is set). Anthropic: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_MODEL (default claude-sonnet-5-5). Groq (free plan): GROQ_API_KEY, GROQ_MODEL (default openai/gpt-oss-120b). Keys never reach the browser.

200.description: The answer, streamed as one JSON event per line.

X-AI-Remaining-Today.description: Questions left today for this user (after this one).

400.description: Invalid body or design. The message names the first problem.

429.description: A limit was reached (per minute, per day, or the app's daily budget), or the AI provider is busy (its own rate limit; the question does not count). `Retry-After` is the exact wait in seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a question is allowed again.

X-AI-Remaining-Today.description: Questions left today for this user (after this one).

502.description: The model failed before replying (bad key, outage).

503.description: The AI Architect is not configured (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or GROQ_API_KEY for the chosen provider).

get.description: How many AI Architect questions the signed-in user has left today (the smaller of their own daily limit and the app's daily budget). The panel shows this as “42 of 50 questions left today”.

configured.description: Whether an AI provider is configured on the server.

sessionCookie.name: next-auth.session-token
sessionCookie.description: NextAuth login token (signed JWT with the user id), set when you sign in. It identifies the user; all user data is read from PostgreSQL.

experienceLevel.description: null until onboarding step 1 is completed

GithubRepo.description: Subset of GitHub's repository object (the full object is returned)

GraphNode.description: One component on the canvas (React Flow node). See docs/graph-spec.md section 2.

implementation.description: component_implementations.id of the chosen technology; omitted means the type's default

properties.description: User overrides, e.g. replicas, capacity, cacheHitRate, authCheckRate, searchRate. Ranges per component type in docs/graph-spec.md section 4.

GraphEdge.description: A connection, pointing in the direction requests flow.

GraphDocument.description: A saved diagram, as defined in docs/graph-spec.md.

customTechnologies.description: Optional. Technologies from an imported repository that the app does not model.

ProjectInput.description: Body of PUT /api/projects/{id}. An `id` field may be included but must match the URL.

updatedAt.description: When the title or diagram last changed
When the title or diagram last changed

nodeId.description: The node it became in the project's graph.

customTechnologies.description: Unknown docker-compose services and app folders in stacks the app does not model (.NET, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, C++). Also saved in project.graph.customTechnologies.

CustomTechnology.description: A technology from an imported repository that ARCHITECH does not model. Listed in the project's sidebar under "From your repo"; dragged onto the canvas it becomes a `custom` node (`data.properties.technology` = name) that Run Design passes traffic through without measuring.

TrafficProfile.description: Load to evaluate the design at, as in Run Design. Every field is optional.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first; starts and ends with a user message.

focus.description: Optional. The part of the canvas the user boxed (selected). The answer explains only that part: its components, how they connect to each other, what comes in from and goes out to the rest of the design, and its role in the whole system. Suggestions may only change selected components, add components, or connect to the selection; others become notes.

DesignChange.description: One operation of a suggested change. Components added by the suggestion are named by refs like "new-cache".

ChatEvent.description: One line of the response stream.

preview.description: suggestion: the engine's numbers before and after applying it
